questions.question: On the number line, which benchmark is 20 closest to?
questions.explain: Count the steps: 20 to 25 is only 5, but 20 to 50 is 30. 25 is closer. A common slip is picking the bigger number, but we want the one that is nearest.

questions.question: Maya has 42 marbles in a cup. She wants to say about how many. Which benchmark is 42 closest to?
questions.explain: Count the steps: 42 to 50 is 8, but 42 to 25 is 17. 50 is closer. The trap is picking 25 because it is the smaller number.

questions.question: There are 18 kids waiting in the gym. Which benchmark is 18 closest to?
questions.explain: Count the steps: 18 to 25 is 7, but 18 to 50 is 32. 25 is closer. Do not jump to 50 just because it is the middle benchmark.

questions.question: A jar has some marbles. The number is closer to 50 than to 100, and it is more than 55. Could it be 60?
questions.explain: Check both clues: 60 to 50 is 10 (closer than 60 to 100, which is 40), and 60 is more than 55. Both fit, so 60 works.

questions.question: A jar has 78 beads. Mia says, '78 is closest to 50.' What did Mia get wrong?
questions.explain: Count the steps: 78 to 100 is 22, but 78 to 50 is 28. So 100 is actually closer. The trap is picking 50 because it is the middle.

questions.question: A basket has some apples. The number is closer to 50 than to 25, and it is more than 45. Could it be 52?
questions.explain: Check both clues: 52 to 50 is only 2 (much closer than 52 to 25, which is 27), and 52 is more than 45. Both fit, so 52 works.

questions.question: A box has some stamps. The number is closer to 100 than to 50, and it is less than 90. Could it be 62?
questions.explain: Check the first clue: 62 to 100 is 38, but 62 to 50 is only 12. So 62 is closer to 50, not 100. The answer is No.

questions.question: On a number line, 47 sits between 25 and 50. Which benchmark is 47 closer to?
questions.explain: 47 is only 3 steps from 50, but 22 steps from 25. On a number line, the closer benchmark is the one with the shorter jump.

questions.question: On a number line, 91 sits between 50 and 100. Which benchmark is 91 closer to?
questions.explain: From 91 it is 9 steps up to 100, but 41 steps back to 50. Count both jumps and pick the small one.

questions.question: On a number line, which number is closer to 25 than to 50?
questions.explain: 29 is just 4 steps past 25, so it stays near 25. The other numbers are past the middle, so they sit closer to 50.

questions.question: A number line goes from 0 to 100. Ivy puts her marker exactly halfway along it. Which benchmark is her marker on?
questions.explain: Half of 100 is 50, so the middle of the line is 50. Watch out: 25 is half of 50, not half of 100.

questions.question: Nina picked 68 blueberries at a farm. She wants to tell her class about how many. Which benchmark should she use?
questions.explain: 68 is 18 more than 50, but it is 32 away from 100, so about 50 fits best. A number can look big and still be closer to 50.

questions.question: Tom has 64 shells in a pail. He is not sure if 64 is closer to 50 or to 100. What is the best way to decide?
options: Pick the first one he said
questions.explain: Find how far 64 is from each benchmark and choose the shorter jump: 14 to 50 and 36 to 100. Being a big number does not make 64 close to 100.

questions.question: Sam counts the buttons in his tin. He says the number is closest to 100. Which number could be in his tin?
questions.explain: 82 is 18 away from 100 and 32 away from 50, so it is closest to 100. Numbers like 68 are still nearer to 50.

questions.question: Ella read 37 pages of her library book. She tells her mom about how many. Which benchmark is 37 closest to?
questions.explain: 37 is 12 past 25 but 13 short of 50, so 25 is a little closer. Always check both jumps before you choose.
